memory_candidates.content: When writing a shell lint that must flag an invocation-path-dependent fixed-depth parent walk (common in a source-store/deployed-tree dual-layout corpus), a naive 'any N+-level walk is forbidden' rule false-positives on real, safe walks that only reach the shallower, invocation-independent boundary (e.g. the extension-root level, which sits at the SAME relative depth below a suite's own directory in both trees). Compute a per-file SAFE_LEVELS boundary from the candidate file's own location instead (e.g. 1 for a flat scripts/*.sh file, 2 for scripts/tests/*.sh), and flag only a walk whose effective depth exceeds that boundary.

A per-line bash-regex lint over a large corpus can approach or exceed its gate timeout budget under concurrent system load even when fast in isolation. Add a cheap `grep -qE` pre-filter per file (matching only the minimal pattern that COULD trigger a violation) before the expensive per-line array-based analysis; this can cut runtime by 5-6x by skipping the vast majority of files that reference the anchor pattern loosely but never the specific violating shape.

deploy-headless.sh's TARGET_REPO defaults to the invoking shell's cwd when no explicit argument is given. Invoking it bare from a non-repository-root cwd (e.g. agent-system/extensions/core/) silently deploys into a stray nested .claude/ tree under that cwd instead of the real repository's .claude/ tree, rather than erroring. Always pass the explicit repository-root TARGET_REPO argument, or invoke from the repository root.
